What is the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis code for this patient?

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY:

Patient:
• Name: Not provided
• Age: 24-year-old
• Gender: Male

Hospitalization Dates:
• Admission: [not provided]
• Discharge: POD #20
Admission Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
• Patient underwent uncomplicated orthotopic liver transplantation after multiple thoracenteses for symtomatic relief of persistent right-sided hepatic hydrothorax.
• Patient presented with respiratory distress and left-sided infiltrates consistent with pneumonia on POD #5 after OLT. Patient was started on antibiotics and underwent a right-sided therapeutic thoracentesis with removal of 1.3 liters of fluid.
• Post-thoracentesis chest imaging revealed a large hydropneumothorax that was treated with a small-bore chest tube.
• Diagnostic bronchoscopy was not performed due to the absence of endobronchial obstruction on CT.
• Patient was stable without dyspnea and hypoxemia, so video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery was deferred after consultation with thoracic surgery.
• Patient was discharged home on POD #20 without supplemental oxygen.
• Follow-up chest x-ray 1 month later showed improvement in the hydropneumothorax and a chest x-ray obtained 6 months later showed near-complete re-expansion of the right lung without surgical intervention.

Discharge Instructions:
• Follow-up with liver transplant team as needed.
• Follow-up with primary care physician for ongoing care.

text:
# ICD-10-AM Principal Diagnosis: **K74.6 – Other and unspecified cirrhosis of liver**

## Why this code

Under ACS 0001 (Principal Diagnosis), the principal diagnosis is the condition that, after study, chiefly caused the admission. This patient was admitted for elective orthotopic liver transplantation (OLT). The condition that made the transplant necessary is end-stage liver disease, which here is presumed to be cirrhosis.

Hepatic hydrothorax is a recognised complication of cirrhosis with portal hypertension. That supports cirrhosis as the underlying disease.

**Important caveat:** The admission diagnosis section is withheld, so the cause of the liver disease is not documented. If the record specifies a cause, use the more specific code instead. Examples:

- K70.3 – Alcoholic cirrhosis
- K74.3–K74.5 – Biliary cirrhosis
- K75.4 – Autoimmune hepatitis
- E83.0 – Wilson disease (worth considering in a 24-year-old)
- B18.x – Chronic viral hepatitis
- K83.0 – Primary sclerosing cholangitis

Clinician clarification should be sought.

## Likely additional diagnoses

| Condition | Suggested code |
|---|---|
| Hepatic hydrothorax | J94.8 – Other specified pleural conditions |
| Pneumonia (POD #5) | J18.9 – Pneumonia, unspecified, plus Y95 if hospital-acquired, per local standards |
| Hydropneumothorax after thoracentesis | J95.8 / T81.x (procedural complication) with the relevant Y-code for misadventure or abnormal reaction, as per ACS 1904 |
| Portal hypertension / ascites, if documented | K76.6 / R18 |

## Key procedures (ACHI)

- Liver transplantation: 90317-00
- Thoracentesis
- Intercostal catheter insertion (small-bore chest tube)

Final code selection depends on review of the complete medical record.
